newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open higher on metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open higher on metal prices.

text.p: Australian shares opened narrowly firmer on Friday with major resource issues buoyed by stronger metal prices. However the broader market was mixed as industrial stocks factored in the effects of a weaker Wall Street close.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 2.7 points up at 2,326.2.
Brokers said the market looked wobbly early, especially as the futures market opened in the opposite direction to the physical market.
The December share price index was three points lower at 2,344 and at a 17.8 point premium to the underlying index.
"Some of the banks have started a bit lower although I think this situation could reverse if the bond market improves over the day," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said healthy buying interest in BHP and CRA was underpinning the market's early gains. BHP was up 19 cents at A$16.48 while CRA was up 36 cents at A$19.20.

The gold sector was also firmer due to a stronger gold price and another solid rise from gold producer Plutonic Resources after its announcement on Thursday of a significant discovery at its Darlot gold mine in Western Australia.
Plutonic shares were 30 cents higher at A$5.75.
"I think we will see the market build on its early gains and maybe finish near its highs today," the dealer said.
